message.content: This file implements the `cat` utility, which concatenates files to standard output. It exports `main` as the program entry point and `fastcat` as an internal function for raw block-based copying. The code relies on standard C library functions (`fopen`, `getc`, `putchar`, `read`, `write`) and system headers (`sys/stat.h`, `sys/types.h`, `sys/param.h`) for file type checks and buffer size constants. A key design decision is the use of a single static buffer in `fastcat` to avoid dynamic allocation overhead, with a `_Static_assert` ensuring the buffer size matches the kernel's `BUFSIZ` and device block size. The `copyopt` function handles all flag-based transformations (numbering, squeezing blanks, showing non-printing characters) by processing input character-by-character, while `fastcat` bypasses all flags for maximum throughput. The program also guards against writing to the same file being read by comparing device and inode numbers via `fstat`.
